messages.author: 0b98505b72b19cfc
messages.subject: High LOD values after permutation.
parts:
Hi,
I know someone else already posted about high LOD values after
permutation, but their response didn't seem to help me. I am working
with a RIL population that has a high marker density (~900), but
limited recombination (the population is small). When I run the
permutation the LOD estimates are ridiculously high, the values range
between 12 and 25. I was using the mqm augmentation (min probability=.
7) with the automatic cofactors option with the data to search for
putative qts, not the scanone function, but I don't think that should
effect the permutation test. I have tried changing my batch size, but
I am new enough to R that I don't know what could be causing it or how
to fix it. If anyone has any suggestions I'd appreciate it. Thanks!

messages.author: 0b98505b72b19cfc
messages.subject: High LOD values after permutation.
parts:
Hi,

I have a RI line population I'm working with in R/qtl. The genetic map
(linkage groups, distances and marker order) is already determined,
and I am trying to identify qtls. I used a combination of the R/qtl
and the MQM function of R/qtl manuals to calculate my genotypic
probabilities, estimate recombination frequencies, impute the missing
genotypes and scan for qtls (using MQM augmentation and the
autocofactor options). I identified qtls with LOD values >5, but they
are not significant after permutation. I have tried doing batch sets,
or the entire dataset all at once, but the confidence values are
always >15 and after 1000 permutations it tends to be around 20. Does
anyone know why this would be happening and if there is something I
can adjust to make a more reasonable LOD? The marker data is pretty
dense (~1 marker <5 cM on average), but I can't imagine that the
marker density is causing this. Has anyone else run into this problem?

Thanks for any suggestions!

Rachel

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] High LOD values after permutation.
parts:
I would look at the scanone results before moving to MQM.

Large LOD thresholds are often due to outliers in the phenotype distribution, but I wouldn't expect them if you have dense and complete genotype information.

karl
